column4: A5-0x5DDB=0x402225 holds the ch2 pressed byte (0x40221C+4*2+1) and is the only input; the earlier capture's posts were FF/FD/EF, i.e. bits 3 and 2 always set, so neither 0x091EAE move.w #1,D1 nor 0x091EBC move.w #0,D1 ever ran and an empty body passed 30/30 (null=30/30). F3_POKE8 is applied once per entry and cannot cycle, so one value is chosen: 0xF7 leaves bit3 clear (D1.w := 1 at 0x091EAE) and bit2 set (the 0x091EBC block is skipped). The D1 difference across calls comes from F3_INJECT_REGS cycling the entry D1 (0x00010005 / 0x0002000A), whose upper half the .w write keeps: post D1 = 0x00010001 / 0x00020001 vs pre 0x00010005 / 0x0002000A, so the null body fails on every pair. The bit2-clear branch (D1.w := 0) is not covered by this one run

column4: the routine ends in `trap #5` at 0x13F462, so it must be driven with F3_INJECT_ABORT: the post is dumped at the 0x13F462 breakpoint (the trap never executes) and the harness then puts PC back to 0x104B8 with the entry SP, which is why 30 pairs accumulate instead of the 1 natural entry fnt_13F436 caught. F3_POKE8=409D1C=00 clears the test-mode byte the 0x13F436 `st.b` sets (0x409D1C = A5+0x1D1C), so that write shows in every pair and an empty body cannot pass; F3_GFX=1 covers the 0x0058AE playfield-3 clear and the 0x005B0C line-RAM rebuild, F3_PAL=1 the move.l #0x60 to palette 0x440000 (poked to FFFFFFFF at entry so that write is never a no-op). F3_NOIRQ keeps VBlank from splitting a pair. Fn_13F436 already matches the register leftovers (D0=0x0018xxxx, D1/D3=0xFFFF, A0=0x5C38, A1=0x621000 from 0x005B0C)
